scope: Original model-loader POSIX file mappings and unlinked regular-file storage in the owned process tree, combined with the observed footprint ledger using an overlap interval. Not arbitrary Apple driver aliases, total physical RAM, a touched working set, or minimum required RAM.
binding_requirement: Before selecting posix-mmap-top-level, retain the actual executable hashes, reference package versions and source/build identities. These source policies do not automatically attest replacement binaries, locally modified packages, different revisions or driver internals.

framework_reference.policy: safetensors initially maps the file through memmap2 for metadata. Its PyTorch mmap backend creates torch.UntypedStorage.from_file(shared=False); PyTorch MapAllocator uses ordinary mmap MAP_PRIVATE and owns the mapping. safetensors retains its active storage in Arc<Storage>; Torch tensors retain their storage. The optional pread backend reads rather than retaining an original-file mapping. The MPS fast path copies source bytes into an owned Shared MTLBuffer and hands it to PyTorch through DLPack; a source checkpoint mapping is not evidence that the destination allocation aliases it. No original model-file submap is explicitly constructed by these loader paths.

llama_cpp_reference.policy: The decoder loader uses ordinary read-only MAP_SHARED mmap when mmap is enabled. Mapped fragments are owned by llama_mmap; model-owned mapped-buffer storage takes ownership of loader mappings. Copied tensor storage is separate from original-file residency. The media/projector loader reads weight bytes into host/backend tensor buffers, using a temporary vector and backend upload when the destination is not host-accessible; it must not be described as the same mmap policy as the decoder.

whisper_cpp_reference.policy: The file initializer opens a binary std::ifstream, feeds loader.read through fin.read and closes the input stream. It is a copied-weight loader, not a persistent checkpoint mmap. Shared Metal buffers own host allocations and wrap them with newBufferWithBytesNoCopy; private buffers use newBufferWithLength. These are allocation-ledger observations, not original GGML-file residency. Closed Metal allocation charging remains an explicit measurement limitation.

limitations: Source mapping provenance alone does not validate a runtime residency query, kernel vnode identity, live process identity, walk completeness or snapshot consistency.

A Metal NoCopy wrapper does not establish that ledger bytes and file-backed resident pages are disjoint. Retain overlap bounds and observed components; do not add independent maxima or mapped lengths.
Driver-created aliases or allocations outside the observed ledger and retained loader mappings are not attested. A valid scoped interval is not a complete physical-memory demand estimate.
